scenes.visual_description: A late Georgian gentleman's club meeting room in London, 1827. A raised Windsor chair sits prominently at the head of the room. Long mahogany tables are cluttered with papers, inkwells, and quill pens. The room is bathed in the warm, slightly smoky glow of oil lamps and candles, casting shadows on the dark wood-panelled walls. The atmosphere is formal yet energetic.

segments.title: CHAPTER II. THE FIRST DAY’S JOURNEY, AND THE FIRST EVENING’S ADVENTURES; WITH THEIR CONSEQUENCES

scenes.visual_description: London, May 1827. Early morning light floods a bustling street lined with brick Georgian terraced houses. In the foreground, a hackney coach stand on cobblestones, with horses and carriages waiting. The atmosphere is hazy and golden. To the side, the exterior of a public house with a wooden sign. The scene captures the transition from dawn to the busy start of a city day.

scenes.location_header: EXT. TOP OF THE COMMODORE COACH - DAY
scenes.visual_description: The open roof of a stagecoach moving through the English countryside. Late morning sun illuminates rolling green hills and hedgerows in the background. In the foreground, the wooden bench seats of the coach roof are visible, piled with luggage and brown paper parcels. The perspective is high and airy, capturing the motion and dust of the road.

scenes.location_header: INT. BULL INN PRIVATE ROOM - EVENING
scenes.visual_description: A private sitting room in an old coaching inn. Late afternoon light fading into evening. Dark mahogany furniture, a table laden with decanters of port wine and dessert plates. A large fireplace with a mantlepiece dominates one wall. Through an open door, a glimpse of a bedroom with a four-poster bed. The mood is warm, convivial, and slightly hazy with tobacco smoke.

A long, elegant Georgian assembly room illuminated by wax candles in glass chandeliers. Crimson-covered benches line the walls. An elevated musicians' gallery overlooks the polished wooden floor. The atmosphere is formal and festive, with warm artificial light reflecting off gilt mirrors and buttoned coats. Shadows gather in the corners where non-dancers observe.

scenes.location_header: INT. BULL INN COFFEE ROOM - MORNING
scenes.visual_description: The coffee room of the Bull Inn. Morning light streams through sash windows, revealing dust motes. Tables are being cleared by servants. A fireplace stands cold. The room feels stark and sober compared to the previous night's festivity. Wooden floorboards and simple sturdy chairs. The mood is tense and hungover.

scenes.location_header: EXT. FIELDS NEAR FORT PITT - DUSK
scenes.visual_description: A secluded grassy field near military fortifications at sunset. The sky is dull and heavy with grey clouds. In the background, the angular earthworks of a fort are visible. A wooden fence and hedge line the perimeter. The light is dimming, creating a sombre, melancholic atmosphere suitable for a duel. A lonely wind ripples the grass.

The owner of the black eyes

scenes.visual_description: A comfortable, old-fashioned private sitting room in the George and Vulture Tavern, London. A roaring fire burns in the grate. The room is furnished with dark wood, heavy curtains, and an easy-chair. A table holds port wine and glasses. The atmosphere is warm, bachelor-like, and secure from the winter night.
A symbolic representation of the book's themes.

A large, bare-looking commercial room in the Peacock Inn, 1827. The atmosphere is dingy and redolent of tobacco smoke. A spacious table sits in the center on an old Turkey carpet. The walls are garnished with maps and weather-beaten greatcoats hanging from pegs. Dusty red curtains shade the windows. Dimly lit by oil lamps and the glow of pipes.

London, May 1827. Early morning light floods a bustling street lined with brick Georgian terraced houses. In the foreground, a hackney coach stand on cobblestones, with horses and carriages waiting. The atmosphere is hazy and golden. To the side, the exterior of a public house with a wooden sign. The scene captures the transition from dawn to the busy start of a city day.

scenes.location_header: INT. BULL INN PRIVATE ROOM - EVENING
scenes.visual_description: A private sitting room in an old coaching inn, bathed in the warm, hazy glow of evening candlelight. Dark mahogany furniture fills the space, including a table laden with decanters of port and brandy. A large fireplace with a mantlepiece dominates one wall. Through an open door, a glimpse of a bedroom with a four-poster bed is visible. The atmosphere is convivial but shadowed, heavy with tobacco smoke and the comfort of travel.

A vast, grassy military review ground in 1827 Rochester, England, under bright midday sun. In the background, lines of soldiers in red coats and white trousers stand in formation, with puffs of white musket smoke drifting in the air. The foreground is packed with a chaotic, dense crowd of Victorian spectators in top hats and bonnets. The atmosphere is dusty, energetic, and slightly overwhelming.

A view from Rochester Bridge in 1827, looking out over the River Medway. In the foreground, the stone balustrades of the bridge. Beyond, the ruined walls of Rochester Castle, crumbling and covered in green ivy, stand against a bright blue sky with light clouds. The river sparkles below, with heavy boats gliding by. Green cornfields and pastures stretch into the distance. Bright, clear morning light.

A bustling Victorian street in the evening outside the Town Arms Inn. Large blue silk flags hang from the windows of the brick facade. A balcony overlooks the street where a crowd gathers. Gas lamps cast a warm glow on cobblestones, while posters cover the walls. The atmosphere is chaotic and political.

A hard, frosty English country road in December, stretching like a block of solid marble. The scene is captured from the top of a moving stagecoach. White breath steams from invisible horses in the crisp air. The landscape is a blur of dry hedges and frozen fields under a clear, cold blue sky. The atmosphere is exhilarating, fast-paced, and biting cold.

A dark, ancient English abbey town street on Christmas Eve. Snow covers the cobblestones and high-gabled roofs. The scene is lit by the warm, orange glow of firelight spilling from cottage windows, contrasting with the cold blue moonlight. The atmosphere is festive but shadowed. In the distance, an old abbey tower rises against the starry night sky. 18th century architecture, wintry and crisp.

scenes.location_header: INT. MR. POTT'S BREAKFAST ROOM - DAY
scenes.visual_description: The breakfast room of a Victorian house, somewhat cluttered with newspapers. Morning light streams onto a table set with Britannia metal pots and toast. The room feels domestic but tense. A fireplace rug dominates the floor. The atmosphere is one of suppressed agitation.

A comfortable, rustic guest bedroom in a large farmhouse. A four-poster bed with heavy curtains dominates the room. A wash-hand basin stands on a wooden dresser. A fireplace is visible. Morning light struggles through the window, suggesting a cold, frosty day outside. 1820s decor. Atmosphere is cold but domestic.

A montage of Victorian legal offices in the Temple. Dark, dirty chambers with low roofs and mouldy walls. Piles of yellowing parchment rolls fill the shelves. The atmosphere is dusty and redolent of dry-rot and tallow candles. 1820s London legal setting.

Mr. Perker's private legal office. A comfortable room with a desk, easy chairs, and a fireplace. Bookshelves line the walls. The atmosphere is confidential and business-like, smelling of snuff and old paper.

Lant Street in the Borough, 1827. A quiet, melancholy back street with green shutters and brass door-plates. Lodging bills hang in windows. The population consists of bookbinders and mantua-makers. The atmosphere is soothingly dull and slightly shabby.

A comfortable upper-floor suite in the Royal Crescent, Bath, 1827. The sitting room is spacious, furnished with Georgian elegance, featuring sash windows that offer a view of the crescent. A writing desk with an inkstand and blotting paper sits near a fireplace. The atmosphere is domestic and slightly aristocratic.

A small, functional room near the stable yard of the Great White Horse Inn. Morning light illuminates a simple table set with a pot of ale, a cold round of beef, and a loaf of bread. The room smells of breakfast and leather. The atmosphere is quiet, save for the sounds of eating and the distant bustle of the inn.

A neat, comfortable first-floor sitting room in 1827 London. A writing desk sits near the window overlooking Goswell Street. A dressing glass stands in the corner. The room is tidy and quiet, furnished with modest but respectable Georgian furniture. Morning light filters through the sash windows. The atmosphere is orderly and domestic.

A bright English countryside scene in early September. Golden stubble fields stretch out towards green hedges and distant hills. A rustic wooden gate stands in the foreground. The sky is a cloudless, brilliant blue. The atmosphere is crisp, sunny, and rural.

scenes.location_header: EXT. FLEET PRISON SKITTLE GROUND - MORNING
scenes.visual_description: The skittle-ground of the Fleet Prison in 1827. A high brick wall forms one side, the prison building the other. The ground is paved, cluttered with racket players and idle prisoners. It is a fine morning with bright sunlight casting shadows on the walls. The atmosphere is lazily chaotic, filled with the sounds of skittles and shouting. Dilapidated but busy.

A courtyard in the City of London, 1827. Morning sunlight strikes the cobblestones. A queer, fresh-painted bright yellow vehicle with black shafts stands out against the dingy surroundings. The atmosphere is urban and busy, with a sense of impending legal trouble.

A bustling inn yard in Whitechapel, London, 1827. Morning light filters through a hazy sky onto cobblestones cluttered with straw and luggage. A stagecoach stands ready, horses being harnessed. The brick facades of the inn surround the yard, with galleries and wooden railings. The atmosphere is busy, noisy, and urban.

A crowded, squalid sleeping ward in the Fleet Prison, 1827. Rows of iron bedsteads are crammed together. Morning light filters through barred, grime-streaked windows, illuminating dirty floorboards and peeling plaster. The atmosphere is stuffy, smelling of close confinement and stale tobacco. A small black portmanteau serves as a seat in the foreground.

The exterior gate of a grand Magistrate's house in Ipswich, 1827. A green gate stands prominently with a bell-handle. Behind it, a flight of steps leads to the house door, guarded by American aloe plants in green tubs. The atmosphere is imposing and official, expecting a riot. Day time.

scenes.location_header: EXT. WHITE HART INN YARD - MORNING
scenes.visual_description: A rambling, tiered inn yard in the Borough, London, 1827. Galleries with clumsy old balustrades run round two sides. Lumbering wagons and heaps of straw fill the cobblestone ground. Morning light filters through a gloomy, antiquated atmosphere. Several boys sleep on wool-packs. The mood is historic and slightly dilapidated.

A lofty, ill-lighted room in Portugal Street, serving as the Insolvent Court. Steam from beer and spirits condenses on the walls. The air is thick with the smell of unwashed bodies and tobacco. Shabby-genteel debtors crowd the enclosure. Gentlemen in wigs sit at desks. The atmosphere is humid, dingy, and hopeless. 1827 London.

A rented private room in the Fleet Prison, 1827. The space is small and dingy, though made tolerably comfortable with hired furniture. A simple table and chairs sit near a sash window that overlooks a brick wall. A candle burns on the table, casting shadows against the peeling wallpaper. The atmosphere is confined but retains a shred of attempted gentility. Nighttime.

scenes.location_header: INT. MR. WINKLE SENIOR'S PARLOUR - NIGHT
scenes.visual_description: A floor-clothed back parlour in a substantial red brick house, half office and half dressing room. A large desk, a high stool, and an iron safe dominate the space. Hanging shelves hold dusty files and an almanac. The room is tidy, business-like, and illuminated by a single oil lamp. 1820s decor.

Goswell Street, London, in July 1827. A hackney cabriolet stands outside a row of brick Georgian houses. One house has a green door, another a yellow, and Mrs. Bardell's has a red one. The street is busy with summer traffic. The atmosphere is fractious and noisy.
London streets at night, 1827. Crowded thoroughfares with men, women, and coaches. Gas lamps cast shadows on the pavement. The atmosphere is hurried and chaotic.

The interior of a small, pretentious medical shop. Gilt-labelled drawers and colored bottles line the walls behind a counter. A glass door leads to a back parlour where a fire burns. The atmosphere is an odd mix of professional facade and chaotic bachelor living. Late afternoon light enters through the shop window.

A lavish late Georgian garden party in bright morning sunlight. A large white marquee stands on a manicured lawn, surrounded by statues and flowerbeds. Crowds of guests in bizarre, colorful fancy dress costumes mingle everywhere. In the background, the white facade of a villa is visible. The atmosphere is chaotic, vibrant, and festive.

A rainy English country road viewed from inside a moving chaise, 1827. Rain streams down the glass windows, blurring the gray, wet landscape outside. Inside, the carriage is damp and cramped. The atmosphere is miserable, wet, and gloomy.
The hallway of the George and Vulture Tavern in London. A window-seat offers a quiet corner. The atmosphere is domestic and slightly flirtatious. 1827 London interior.

scenes.location_header: INT. OSBORNE'S HOTEL EATING ROOM - DAY
scenes.visual_description: A small eating-room in Osborne's Hotel. A simple table is set with a meat-pie, steak, and porter. The room is functional, with wainscoted walls and a sideboard. Less elegant than the private sitting room. 1827 hotel interior.

A small, cozy room behind the bar of the Marquis of Granby inn, Dorking. Morning light filters through red curtains. A fire burns in the grate. A round table and chairs sit near the fire. The room smells of stale tobacco and spirits. Victorian roadside tavern interior.

A dark, mouldy, earthy-smelling ground-floor office in 1820s London. High wainscotted partitions divide the room. The foreground features old wooden chairs and desks cluttered with dirty bundles of papers and decayed stone ink bottles. A loud-ticking clock hangs on the wall. The only light comes from a glass door leading to a passage. The atmosphere is dingy, bureaucratic, and secluded.

The steep, narrow Canongate of Edinburgh on a wild, windy night in the 1820s. Tall, gaunt tenements, six or seven stories high, loom against a dark, cloud-swept sky. A few oil lamps sputter in the gloom, revealing rough cobblestones and dark alley entrances. Shadows are deep and shifting. The atmosphere is ghostly, historic, and desolate.

A magistrate's study in a grand Ipswich house. A large easy-chair sits behind a heavy desk laden with legal papers. The room is imposing, with bookshelves and portraits of authority figures. Sunlight streams in, illuminating dust motes. The atmosphere is pompous and judicial.

scenes.location_header: INT. ANGEL INN PRIVATE ROOM - EVENING
scenes.visual_description: A comfortable private sitting-room in the Angel Inn, Bury St. Edmunds. Heavy mahogany furniture and a well-set dinner table occupy the center. Sash windows overlook the street. The room is illuminated by wax candles, creating a warm, domestic, yet slightly conspiratorial atmosphere suitable for private dining.

scenes.location_header: EXT. TOP OF THE COMMODORE COACH - DAY
scenes.visual_description: The open roof of a stagecoach moving through the English countryside. Late morning sun illuminates rolling green hills and hedgerows in the background. In the foreground, the wooden bench seats of the coach roof are visible, piled with luggage and brown paper parcels. The perspective is high and airy, capturing the motion and dust of the road.

A small, cluttered front parlour in Goswell Street. The room is lit by two candles and the glow of a fire. A Dutch oven sits before the grate, browning cheese. A tin saucepan simmers on the hob. Shadows dance on the walls. The atmosphere is intimate, domestic, and redolent of gossip and supper.

A small, picturesque English country town High Street in the late 18th century. Quaint brick houses with bow windows line the street. A small church spire is visible in the distance. The atmosphere is quiet, sleepy, and idyllic. Soft afternoon sunlight illuminates the dusty road and the saddler's shop with its hanging sign.

The busy hallway of a coaching inn. Wooden floorboards are scuffed from heavy traffic. The walls are plastered and hung with election notices. Servants bustle past carrying trays. A smell of stale beer and tobacco hangs in the air. Lighting is dim, provided by oil lamps.
A fashionable square in Bath at evening. Elegant Georgian townhouses line the square. A lamp-post stands on the pavement, against which a footman leans. The atmosphere is quiet, urban, and expectant.

The entrance hall and staircase area of the Fleet Prison. Stone steps lead up from the yard. The walls are grimy and peeling. A few prisoners loiter. The lighting is dim, provided by dust-moted daylight from the door. The atmosphere is institutional and echoing.

A close view of an open barouche carriage parked on the grass, 1827. The horses are removed. A large wicker hamper spills cold fowls, wine bottles, and crockery onto the carriage seats. Seated are Victorian ladies in scarfs and feathers and gentlemen in blue coats. The setting is a picnic within a crowd, with the military review visible in the blurred distance. Sunlight glints off wine glasses and brass buttons.

A bustling London street near Newgate Market in 1827. A pork shop stands prominently with a display of sausages. The street is lined with brick buildings and busy with morning traffic. The atmosphere is crisp and urban. Pedestrians in Victorian dress hurry by.

The bustling street outside the Bull Inn, Rochester, 1827. A curious little green chaise with four wheels stands on the cobblestones, hitched to an immense brown horse. The brick facade of the inn is visible, with coffee-room blinds in the windows. A stable yard atmosphere with hostlers and horses. Morning sunlight casts sharp shadows on the pavement.

A bustling, somewhat dirty street in Bristol, 1827. Narrow pavements wind between mix of commercial and residential buildings. A newly painted tenement stands out with a red lamp projecting over the fanlight. Gold lettering on a wainscot ground reads 'Surgery'. Afternoon light filters through the haze of a busy port city.

The cozy, warm bar of the Marquis of Granby inn. A large fireplace with a kettle singing on the hob dominates the room. High-backed chairs sit on either side, one designated for the landlord. The bar window displays geraniums and spirit phials. The atmosphere is snug, domestic, and scented with tea, toast, and pine-apple rum. Victorian roadside tavern style.

scenes.location_header: INT. BUSH INN COFFEE ROOM - EVENING
scenes.visual_description: A traditional coffee room in the Bush Inn, Bristol. A coal fire burns in the grate, casting a warm glow on the mahogany tables and windsor chairs. High-backed partitions offer privacy. The room is quiet, with evening shadows lengthening in the corners. 1827 decor.

A private sitting room in the Great White Horse Inn, bright with morning light. A breakfast table sits at the upper end. The room features standard inn furniture: a few chairs, a table, and a window recess. The atmosphere is initially calm, contrasting with the tension of the occupants.

A crowded dining hall inside a Victorian villa, bustling with activity. A long mahogany table is laden with lobster salads, jellies, and wine bottles. Guests in fancy dress are packed together, eating and talking. Large French windows open onto the sunlit gardens. The atmosphere is stifling, noisy, and busy.

The crowded, imposing interior of the Guildhall Court of Common Pleas. A high wooden bench for the judge dominates the room, surmounted by the Royal Arms. Below, the clerk's table and the well of the court are packed with wigged barristers. A wooden jury box stands to the side. A gallery above is filled with spectators. Dusty shafts of light cut through the stuffy, hazy air. The atmosphere is formal, tense, and heavy with legal procedure.

The cramped, dark interior of a travelling chaise at night. Flashes of lantern light streak across the rain-streaked glass windows. Worn leather seats and velvet padding are visible in the gloom. The atmosphere is chaotic and motion-blurred, with deep shadows and cold blue moonlight occasionally cutting through heavy clouds. Mud splatters against the glass.

A long, low-roofed parlour in the Leather Bottle Inn, Cobham, 1827. Heavy wooden beams cross the ceiling. High-backed, leather-cushioned chairs of fantastic shapes line the plaster walls, which are embellished with dark old portraits. A table at the upper end is covered with a white cloth, roast fowl, and ale. Warm, antiquated atmosphere.

A dingy, uncomfortable travellers' room in a London coaching inn. The space is divided into wooden boxes for the solitary confinement of travellers. A kitchen fireplace dominates the room, complete with a rebellious poker. A small washing-kennel for glasses sits in the corner. The atmosphere is damp, mouldy, and redolent of human dejection. 1820s decor.

A view from a moving chaise-cart travelling along the London Road. The English countryside rolls by in the background. The foreground shows the driver's bench. The atmosphere is transitional and open. 1827.

scenes.location_header: INT. OSBORNE'S HOTEL SITTING ROOM - DAY
scenes.visual_description: A private sitting room in Osborne's Hotel, Adelphi, 1827. A comfortable, carpeted room with a sofa and mahogany furniture. Sash windows overlook the street. Doors lead to adjacent bedrooms. The atmosphere is domestic yet transient, typical of a high-end coaching hotel. Afternoon light.

A solemn, frozen churchyard at night. Ancient, leaning tombstones are covered in sparkling hoar frost. The old stone church casts a long, deep shadow. The moon is young and dim, shedding pale, ghostly light on the snow. The atmosphere is silent, cold, and eerie. A partially dug grave disrupts the smooth white blanket of snow. 18th century setting.
A hallway in the George and Vulture Tavern. Wooden floorboards, gas lamps, and numbered doors. A waiter leads a guest. The atmosphere is quiet and domestic. 1827.

A romantic Victorian garden arbour at twilight, dense with honeysuckle and jessamine. Deep green shadows envelop a rustic wooden bench within the bower. A large watering pot lies on the grass path. The sky above is a deepening violet as evening sets in, contrasting with the dark, leafy foliage. The atmosphere is intimate, secluded, and heavy with sentiment.

The Lodge of the Fleet Prison. A small, functional room with a grated window overlooking the prison interior. A large desk supports a heavy registry book. The walls are hung with keys and notices. The atmosphere is bureaucratic and indifferent. 1820s office decor with a worn, grimy feel.

scenes.location_header: INT. WHITE HART PRIVATE ROOM - MORNING
scenes.visual_description: A private sitting-room in the White Hart Inn. A breakfast table is set with coffee and rolls. Sash windows overlook the yard. The furniture is worn but respectable, typical of a coaching inn. Morning light streams in, illuminating dust motes. The atmosphere is domestic yet transient.

The open roof of a stagecoach moving through the outskirts of London. The road is busy with traffic. In the background, rows of brick houses give way to turnpikes and open road. The sky is bright and cloudy. The mood is transitional, moving from city congestion to travel.

The Great Pump Room in Bath, a spacious saloon with Corinthian pillars and a high ceiling. A music gallery overlooks the room. A Tompion clock and a statue of Nash are prominent. A large bar with a marble vase dispenses water into yellow-looking tumblers. The atmosphere is polite, crowded with invalids and fashionables.

A bustling, slightly seedier public house interior at night. Saffron-hued curtains hang in the windows. A long mahogany table is crowded with clerks drinking and smoking. Gas lamps cast a yellow, hazy glow through the thick tobacco smoke. The atmosphere is rowdy, convivial, and distinctly legal-clerk oriented.

A gloomy winter's evening on the Marlborough Downs. A miry, sloppy road stretches across the open plain. Heavy rain slants down, driven by a fierce wind. The landscape is dark, wet, and desolate, illuminated only by the faint light of a gig's lanterns. The atmosphere is cold, blustery, and miserable.

The outer office of a solicitor in Gray's Inn. The room is dingy and functional, with a large fire burning. A clerk's desk is cluttered with papers. The door leads to a dark, draughty staircase. The atmosphere is professional but worn and dusty.

A private sitting room in the Saracen's Head Inn, Towcester. A bright fire burns in the grate, contrasting with the storm outside. The room is furnished with a table set for dinner, heavy curtains drawn against the night, and comfortable chairs. The atmosphere is warm, domestic, and relieved.

A damp, rotting set of chambers in an ancient inn, long shut up and empty. The room is scantily furnished with a few chairs and a large, lumbering wooden press with glass doors and a green curtain. A fire burns in the grate, casting flickering shadows on the mouldering fixtures. The atmosphere is eerie, dusty, and unnaturally still.

A grassy knoll dominated by a massive, ancient oak tree providing deep shade. Below, a patchwork of arable meadow land and luxuriant hedges spreads out to the horizon. A picnic lunch is spread on the grass with stone bottles and woven baskets. Dappled sunlight filters through the leaves.

A respectable but severe Victorian law office on the first floor. A black writing desk dominates the center, covered in legal papers. The room is tidy but soulless, with dark mixture trousers and black gaiters visible as details of the occupant. The lighting is functional and stark. The atmosphere is oppressive and stern.

Mr. Bob Sawyer's first-floor front room, prepared for a bachelor party. A small table with a green baize cloth sits in the center. Mismatched glasses are arranged on a tray. A coal fire burns in the grate. The room is cluttered, comfortable, and smells of punch and tobacco smoke.

A back parlour in a public house opposite the Insolvent Court. The room is smoky and crowded with coachmen and shady legal types. Wooden tables are sticky with beer rings. A smell of shrimps and porter fills the air. The atmosphere is convivial but slightly seedy.

A quiet, retired courtyard near St. Clement's Church in Ipswich. Ancient brick houses line the perimeter. A green garden gate stands at the bottom of the yard. The area is secluded and venerable, with a sense of hidden activity. Morning sunlight casts shadows on the paving stones.

A small, cozy room behind the bar of the Marquis of Granby inn, Dorking. A fire burns in the grate, casting a warm glow on the red curtains. A round table and chairs sit near the fire. The room smells of stale tobacco and spirits, with a mournful, quiet atmosphere due to the recent funeral.

A miserable, bare room in the Fleet Prison at night. A rough deal table dominates the center, with a rush-candle burning on the floor underneath it, glowing like a red-hot coal. A mattress lies on the floorboards. Shadows are long and heavy, obscuring the peeling walls. The atmosphere is stifling, poverty-stricken, and eccentric. 1820s.

A cheerful, elegant study in a new villa at Dulwich, 1828. A large bay window opens onto a sunny lawn and manicured garden. The room is filled with comfortable easy-chairs, odd cabinets, and walls lined with books and pictures. Sunlight floods the space, illuminating rich carpets and curtains. The atmosphere is peaceful, domestic, and retired. Warm browns, greens, and gold tones.

The interior of a debtor's prison cell in the early 19th century. Bare, peeling walls enclose a small, stifling space. A simple cot and a few worn items of furniture constitute the home. High, barred windows let in a sliver of grey light. The atmosphere is oppressive, hopeless, and squalid, smelling of poverty and confinement.

A secluded, cozy parlour in the Blue Boar Inn, Leadenhall Market. A small coal fire burns in a grate, guarded by a poker. A wooden box-seat is positioned near the stove. A simple table is dusted clean, holding an inkstand and a glass of brandy. The room is dim, private, and smells of spirits and tobacco. 1820s tavern interior.

A homely, smoke-filled tavern room in London, 1827. Wooden boxes or booths with tables line the walls. The room is thick with tobacco smoke. Pewter quart pots sit on the tables. The atmosphere is warm, brown, and working-class, patronized by heavy-coated stage-coachmen.

The same sitting room in the Royal Crescent at night. The room is quiet, lit by the warm glow of a fire and a single bedroom candle on the desk. Shadows play on the walls. The atmosphere is solitary and peaceful.

A desolate piece of waste ground in Edinburgh at night. The skeletal remains of old mail coaches stand huddled together, stripped of linings and wheels. Rain drips from their rotting roofs. A rough wooden fence surrounds the enclosure. The moon casts pale, eerie light on the decaying woodwork. The atmosphere is melancholic and abandoned.

A bustling London street in the damp, drizzly morning mist. A stagecoach stands ready, its door emblazoned with gilt lettering. The horses steam in the cold air. Porters struggle with luggage on the wet cobblestones. The atmosphere is muggy, chaotic, and urban. 1827.

A rustic village green in the late afternoon. In the center stands the Pound, a small wooden enclosure for stray animals, currently holding a wheelbarrow. Quaint cottages and a church spire are visible in the background. The scene is public and slightly humiliating.

A quiet, secluded back lane in Clifton, Bristol. High brick garden walls line both sides, concealing villas. Overhanging trees cast dappled shadows. A green stable door stands at the bottom of the lane, with a large stone opposite. Afternoon sunlight.

The cobblestone stable yard of the Angel Inn in bright morning sunlight. A wooden pump stands prominently in the foreground with a trough. Benches line the walls where hostlers sit. The brick facade of the inn rises around the yard. The atmosphere is fresh and busy with morning stable activities.

A small, humble parlour behind a greengrocer's shop. Two mismatched tables are pushed together, covered with cloths of varying whiteness. The cutlery is eclectic with green, red, and yellow handles. A fire burns in the grate. The room is crowded with footmen in brilliant, colorful liveries (crimson, orange, blue, purple) which contrast absurdly with the modest surroundings.

A front parlour in Coleman Street converted into a temporary lock-up. Fresh sand covers the floor, but the air is thick with stale tobacco smoke. Barred windows admit grey London light. The furniture is worn and dirty. The atmosphere is depressing, smelling of gin and confinement.

scenes.location_header: EXT. GREAT WHITE HORSE INN - EVENING
scenes.visual_description: The exterior of the Great White Horse Inn in Ipswich at evening. A massive, imposing brick building with a stone statue of an insane-looking cart-horse over the principal door. The street is dimming into twilight. The inn looks labyrinthine and slightly mouldy. Atmosphere is heavy and antiquated.

scenes.location_header: INT. WHITE HART EMPTY ROOM - DAY
scenes.visual_description: A bare, dusty apartment in the White Hart Inn. An empty grate and a few stiff-backed chairs are the only furniture. A window offers a view of the yard. The walls are bare and the floorboards creak. The atmosphere is quiet, conspiratorial, and slightly stark.
A private sitting room in the hotel. A work table is set out. The room is modest but comfortable. Arabella sits at work. 1827.

The large, stone-flagged kitchen of the Saracen's Head Inn. A massive fireplace with a settling bench dominates the room. Copper pots gleam on the walls in the firelight. The room is warm and shadowed, smelling of woodsmoke and cooking. A rougher, more communal space than the private room.

A muddy English country road at grey dawn. The shattered remains of a wooden chaise carriage lie on its side in the foreground, wheels broken and axle snapped. Mists rise from the surrounding wet fields and hedgerows. The light is flat, cold, and colourless, emphasizing the mud and disarray of the accident. A second carriage stands in the distance.

A snug, comfortable old parlour in a roadside inn. A roaring fire burns in the grate, casting a warm red glow. A bar window is visible, reflecting rows of green bottles and gold labels. A table is set with a clean white cloth. The atmosphere is cozy and inviting, contrasting with the storm outside.

Fleet Street, London, 1827. A busy thoroughfare crowded with pedestrians, carriages, and carts. The noise of wheels and hooves is constant. A procession of coachmen makes its way through the crowd. The atmosphere is chaotic and urban.

The same rented room in the Fleet Prison, now flooded with grey morning light. A breakfast table is set with white linens and a meat-pie. Clothes and gaiters are laid out for brushing. The room feels busier and slightly more hopeful than at night, though still grimly enclosed by the prison walls.

The street outside the Marquis of Granby inn at night. A horse-trough stands full of water in the foreground. The inn's windows are dim. The atmosphere is energetic and chaotic as a man is kicked into the street.

scenes.location_header: INT. TOWN ARMS COMMITTEE ROOM - NIGHT
scenes.visual_description: A large private room on the first floor of the inn, converted into a committee room. A long table is covered with books, papers, and inkwells. The room is well-lit by candles. Heavy curtains are drawn. The atmosphere is conspiratorial and busy.

The interior of a cramped stagecoach moving through the English countryside. Worn upholstery lines the seats. Through the windows, a blur of rain and passing landscapes is visible. The atmosphere is companionable but confined. 1827.

A small, enclosed room within the prison serving as a private bar or 'snuggery'. Wooden tables and chairs are crammed in. The room smells of stale tobacco and spirits. Dim light filters through a small window. It feels cozy but seedy, a refuge for the wealthier prisoners.

A dusty English country road winding through hedges and green hills in 1827. The perspective is from the road level, emphasizing the track and the surrounding vegetation. White clouds drift in a blue sky. The scene is bright but implies the chaotic motion of travel. No buildings visible, just the open road and nature.

A small, private antechamber opening off the main justice-parlour. It is sparsely furnished but respectable, intended for confidential legal discussions. A half-closed door connects to the larger room. The atmosphere is secretive and hushed.

The roadside exterior of the Marquis of Granby inn in Dorking. A large sign-board on a high post depicts the Marquis. A horse trough and stable door are visible. Clean windows display geraniums. The atmosphere is thriving and roadside-bucolic. Morning light hits the red brick facade and the dusty road.

A quaint English village street in Cobham, 1827. In the foreground, a rustic cottage door with a small stone step. A broken stone lies half-buried in the dirt near the threshold. The red brick facade of the Leather Bottle Inn is visible nearby. Afternoon sunlight hits the thatched roofs and cobblestones. Rural and historic.

The main street of the corporate town of Muggleton in 1827. Red brick Georgian houses and shops line the street, including a large inn with a sign displaying a Blue Lion. Shop windows display bonnets and saddles. The architecture is solid and provincial. The atmosphere is busy with the anticipation of the cricket match. Bright midday sun.

scenes.location_header: EXT. FIELDS NEAR MANOR FARM - TWILIGHT
scenes.visual_description: A country lane at twilight, the air fine, dry, and bracingly cold. The grass is crisp with frost, and the sky is a deep slate-colour. A wooden stile stands in the foreground, separating the lane from open fields. The atmosphere is energetic and cheerful, with the gray light of winter evening settling over the hedgerows.

A bustling English street in Bury St. Edmunds, late afternoon. The facade of the Angel Inn rises in the background. Pedestrians in Victorian dress move along the cobblestones. The atmosphere is busy and purposeful as the sun begins to lower.

A vast, subterranean cavern with walls of dark, rough-hewn rock. The space is illuminated by a strange, supernatural reddish glow, perhaps from a central fire or the goblins themselves. In the center, an elevated stone seat or throne. The atmosphere is oppressive, magical, and terrifying. Shadows dance on the walls, suggesting a crowd of unseen creatures.

The Spaniards Tea-gardens in Hampstead. A pleasant outdoor venue with gravel paths, arbours, and tables set for tea. Summer foliage is lush. The atmosphere is festive but marred by family squabbles. Waiters bustle with tea-trays.

A lush green meadow on a summer's evening, bathed in the golden light of sunset. Hedgerows full of wildflowers border the field. Long shadows stretch across the grass. The atmosphere is romantic, calm, and pastoral, with the sounds of birds settling for the night.

A substantial dining room in Manor Farm. A large mahogany table is set for lunch with strong beer and cherry-brandy. The room is warm, wood-panelled, and decorated for Christmas. Portraits of ancestors hang on the walls. The atmosphere is heavy with food and comfort. 1820s style.

A comfortable dining room in a Russell Square townhouse, 1827. The table is strewn with the remnants of a dinner party—wine glasses, decanters, and fruit. A kitchen candle provides dim, shadowy illumination, contrasting with the unseen brightness of the drawing room. The atmosphere is conspiratorial and post-festive.

A lush English country garden in bright morning sunlight, shortly after sunrise. The red brick facade of Manor Farm rises in the background, with an open lattice window visible on the upper floor. Hay-ricks and deep-green meadows stretch out beyond the manicured garden. Dew glistens on flower petals and leaves. The atmosphere is fresh, vibrant, and pastoral.

A large, badly-furnished private apartment in the Great White Horse Inn. A dirty grate holds a small, wretched fire. The room is dim, lit by candles and the fire's weak glow. Heavy, worn furniture and a table with the remains of dinner and a bottle of port. The atmosphere is dispiriting and dingy.

The bustling streets of Ipswich in broad daylight. Georgian brick buildings line the road. A crowd fills the cobblestone street. A sedan chair is the focal point. The atmosphere is chaotic, noisy, and riotous.

A lavish Victorian drawing room in Ipswich. The decor is ostentatious, with pink gauze drapery and heavy furniture. Mirrors reflect the agitation of the occupants. The room is designed to impress local society, filled with the tension of a family crisis. Late afternoon light.

A small, humble cottage interior, neat and clean. A bright fire burns in the hearth, casting a warm, cozy light on modest wooden furniture and a frugal meal spread on a table. The room feels intimate and loving. 18th century rural domestic style. The atmosphere is one of simple happiness and comfort despite poverty.

A large frozen pond in the grounds of Manor Farm, surrounded by snow-covered trees and fields. The ice is swept clean in patches for skating. In the background, the red brick farmhouse is visible. The sky is a crisp, cold blue. The atmosphere is energetic and wintery, with figures skating and sliding. 1827 English countryside.

A large, stuffy meeting room located at the top of a steep ladder in Brick Lane. A table covered in green baize stands in the center, bearing a conspicuous wooden money-box. Wooden forms line the walls, crowded with people. Candlelight casts long, dancing shadows on the peeling plaster walls. The atmosphere is chaotic, righteous, and thick with humidity.

The Royal Crescent, Bath, at 3 AM on a windy night. The curved row of grand Georgian houses stands dark and silent. The wind sweeps furiously around the high ground, threatening to tear up paving stones. A sedan chair sits on the cobblestones, lit by the flaring torch of a link-boy. Atmosphere is cold, blustery, and chaotic.

A section of a high brick garden wall at dusk. A large pear tree extends its boughs over the coping. A gravel path and a garden seat are visible inside the wall. The light is dim and purple-hued. Atmosphere is romantic but shadowed.

A comfortable hotel bedroom at night. A four-poster bed dominates the room. A door with brass fittings stands closed. Candlelight flickers, illuminating the washstand and a chair where clothes are piled. The atmosphere is quiet until disturbed.

A private room in the sheriff officer's house. Better furnished than the coffee room, with a carpet, table, chairs, sideboard, and sofa. A looking-glass and old prints decorate the walls. Sounds of a piano drift from overhead. The atmosphere is respectable but constrained.

A small, filthily dirty room in the prison. Three rolled-up mattresses occupy a corner. The floor is scattered with remnants of food, broken crockery, and damp towels. There is no carpet or curtain. The air smells intolerably close. A window looks down onto the parade. 1820s squalor.

A large, desolate infirmary ward in the Fleet Prison at night. Rows of iron stump bedsteads stretch into the gloom. A single window stands open, letting in the distant roar of the city. The room is bare and cold, lit by a dim lantern. The atmosphere is heavy with sickness, stagnation, and impending death. 1820s.

The main tap-room of the prison. Crowded, noisy, and smelling of beer. Rough wooden benches and tables. Gas lamps might be unlit during the day, leaving the room in a brown, hazy gloom. The atmosphere is boisterous and communal.

The interior of a hackney coach. Cramped, dark, and swaying. Mrs. Bardell, Mrs. Cluppins, Mrs. Sanders, and Mr. Jackson are squeezed inside. Through the windows, the road passes by. The atmosphere is tense and sleepy.

The same yard transformed into a bustling coaching hub at night. The mail coaches are restored to pristine condition, lamps blazing with light. Horses are harnessed, and luggage is piled high. The scene is vibrant and crowded with activity, lit by the warm glow of carriage lamps against the dark night. 18th-century styling.

A stockbroker's office on a first floor near the Bank of England. The room is cluttered with papers wafered against the walls. A desk and high stools are occupied by flashy gentlemen. The atmosphere is casual, betting-oriented, and dusty. 1827.
The courtyard of the George and Vulture Tavern. Cobblestones, stable doors, and the back entrance to the inn. The atmosphere is secluded. 1827.

A long, elegant Georgian assembly room illuminated by wax candles in glass chandeliers. Crimson-covered benches line the walls. An elevated musicians' gallery overlooks the polished wooden floor. The atmosphere is formal and festive, with warm artificial light reflecting off gilt mirrors and buttoned coats. Shadows gather in the corners where non-dancers observe.

A dilapidated roadside public house in the English countryside. Two large elm trees and a horse trough stand in front. The building is weathered, with rotten sheds and mouldering outhouses jumbled nearby. A kitchen garden is visible to the side. The atmosphere is quiet, rural, and slightly run-down. Late afternoon light.

A cozy, old-fashioned Victorian parlour at night, bathed in the warm, golden glow of a roaring fire and wax candles. Dark oak panelling lines the walls, adorned with samplers and portraits. In the foreground, card tables with playing cards are set out. Comfortable armchairs surround the hearth. The atmosphere is festive, domestic, and rich with history.

A traditional English cricket field on a village green. Two large white canvas marquees (tents) stand on the grass. In the distance, wickets are pitched. Men in white flannel jackets and straw hats dot the green. The foreground features the entrance to one of the tents, with wooden benches and refreshments visible inside. Sunny, festive atmosphere.

A small, shadowed bedroom in the Leather Bottle Inn at night. A lattice window stands open to the darkness. A single candle burns low in a socket on a small table, casting flickering shadows on a simple four-poster bed. The corners of the room are lost in gloom. Atmosphere is eerie, solitary, and tense.

A domestic Victorian parlour, somewhat cluttered. A window looks out onto the street. A round table is set for cards near the fireplace. Portraits of stern ancestors line the walls. The room feels lived-in and slightly oppressive. Candlelight flickers against dark wallpaper.

A large, rambling bedroom in an old inn. A roaring fire burns in the grate. The room features big closets, oaken presses, and a huge bed. Prominent in the room is a strange, grim-looking, high-backed chair carved with a human face. Shadows from the fire dance on the walls. The atmosphere is mysterious and slightly eerie.

A convivial taproom in the Angel Inn, scented with spirits and cloves. Pewter vessels and glasses sit on wooden tables. The room is dim and cozy, with daylight filtering through small windows. Wooden benches and a sawdust-covered floor complete the rustic, traditional pub setting.

A rich, old-fashioned parlour in a prosperous saddler's house. A large iron safe is built into the wall over the chimney-piece. Dark polished wood furniture, a roaring fire, and heavy curtains create a cozy but slightly oppressive atmosphere. The table is set with real silver and china. Candlelight flickers on the walls.

A steep, dirty wooden staircase inside a legal inn of court at night. The area is dimly lit, with shadows clinging to the peeling paint. A heavy outer door labeled 'MR. PERKER' stands closed on a landing. The atmosphere is quiet, deserted, and slightly grim.

A wild, lonely spot beneath towering cliffs at sunset. The ocean stretches out to the horizon, stained a deep crimson by the setting sun. Large fragments of fallen rock litter the beach. The atmosphere is dramatic, isolated, and foreboding, with long shadows cast by the frowning cliffs above.

A solicitor's office, cluttered with papers, deed boxes, and piles of documents. A large desk dominates the room. Dust motes dance in the light from a street-facing window. The room is functional and dry. The atmosphere is mercenary and business-like.

A late Georgian gentleman's club meeting room in London, 1827. A raised Windsor chair sits prominently at the head of the room. Long mahogany tables are cluttered with papers, inkwells, and quill pens. The room is bathed in the warm, slightly smoky glow of oil lamps and candles, casting shadows on the dark wood-panelled walls. The atmosphere is formal yet energetic.

The Counsel's Office at the Bank of England. A long counter with a round blackboard featuring a large 'W'. Clerks sit behind the counter eating ham sandwiches. The room is bureaucratic, busy, and echoes with the noise of the courtyard. 1827.

The interior of an 18th-century mail coach. Plush velvet seats and leather trimmings are visible in the dim, shaking light. A window looks out into darkness. The space is cramped and intimate. The atmosphere is tense and mysterious, occupied by passengers in antique dress.

The exterior gate of the Fleet Prison. A large, forbidding wall with a heavy gate. Crowds of wan, emaciated debtors press towards the exit. Afternoon light filters into the lodge area. The atmosphere is one of release and lingering melancholy.

A prisoner's private room converted into a secret gin shop. A messy bedstead dominates the space. A flat stone bottle is hidden underneath. The room is untidy, with uncombed vibes. Dim, secretive lighting. The atmosphere is illicit and hushed.

A solitary room in the Fleet, furnished with the barest necessities. A tottering table and a few rickety chairs stand on bare floorboards. The room feels empty and desolate, reflecting years of privation. Light enters through a single window, highlighting the dust. The atmosphere is silent and melancholic.
A low archway entrance to a legal inn off Fleet Street. A stream of lawyers and clerks pours in and out. Shabby-genteel men loiter in the shadows. The atmosphere is bustling, legalistic, and dingy.

The Clifton lane in pitch darkness. The scene is illuminated only by a sharp, circular beam from a dark lantern, cutting through the gloom to hit wet cobblestones or brickwork. Deep shadows surround the small tunnel of light. Atmosphere of stealth and comedy.

A tolerably large double-bedded room in the inn. A fire burns in the grate. Two four-poster beds with heavy curtains stand on opposite sides. A rush-bottomed chair and a dressing table with a mirror are visible. Candlelight flickers against dark wainscoting. Comfortable but old-fashioned.

A walled garden at night, plunged in deep shadow. A high brick wall looms on one side. Gooseberry bushes and rose trees clutter the foreground. The sky is heavy with storm clouds, occasionally lit by vivid flashes of lightning. Rain slickens the gravel paths. The mood is tense, dark, and ominous.

A private sitting-room in the White Hart Hotel, Bath. Elegant Georgian furniture fills the space. A breakfast table is cleared of china. Sash windows overlook the street. The room is bright, fashionable, and well-appointed. The atmosphere is polite and expectant.

A lush, vibrant English landscape in high summer. A clear blue sky hangs over sparkling water and green trees. Flowers bloom in bright colors. The sun shines brilliantly, casting dappled light through leaves. The atmosphere is idyllic, cheerful, and full of life. A stark contrast to the winter scenes.

A large, stone-flagged kitchen in the basement of the Magistrate's house. A huge dresser is filled with china. A clean jack towel hangs behind the door. A sink with water laid on is visible. The atmosphere is warm, smelling of dinner preparation and yellow soap. Servants' domain.

A large private dining room in the Blue Lion Inn. A long mahogany table is cluttered with the remnants of a feast: empty wine bottles, fruit bowls, and crumpled napkins. Wax candles in sconces provide a warm, smoky light against dark panelled walls. The atmosphere is convivial, hazy with tobacco smoke, and festive.

A cheerful Victorian breakfast parlour flooded with late morning light. A chintz sofa sits prominently in the foreground. Through the windows, the garden is visible. The room is decorated with floral wallpaper and family portraits. A breakfast table is set with white linens and silver, though currently neglected. The mood is domestic but slightly chaotic.

A spacious, welcoming farmhouse kitchen at Manor Farm. A large fireplace with a roaring wood fire dominates the room, despite it being May. The red brick floor glows in the firelight. Hams, sides of bacon, and ropes of onions hang from the ceiling beams. Hunting whips, bridles, and an old blunderbuss decorate the walls. Warm, rustic, and domestic atmosphere.

scenes.location_header: INT. BULL INN COFFEE ROOM - MORNING
scenes.visual_description: The coffee room of the Bull Inn. Morning light streams through sash windows, revealing dust motes. Tables are being cleared by servants. A fireplace stands cold. The room feels stark and sober compared to the previous night's festivity. Wooden floorboards and simple sturdy chairs. The mood is tense and hungover.

scenes.location_header: INT. MR. POTT'S GUEST ROOM - NIGHT
scenes.visual_description: A guest bedroom in deep shadow. A four-poster bed dominates the space. Moonlight filters faintly through curtains. The room is quiet and still, contrasting with the earlier noise. Dark furniture looms in the corners.

A long, dark-panelled room at Manor Farm, transformed for a ball. A massive fireplace with a high chimney-piece dominates one wall, filled with a blazing log fire. Recesses hold massive old silver candlesticks with four branches each. At the upper end, a bower of holly and evergreens shelters musicians. The floor is bare wood, stripped of carpets for dancing. Warm, festive, and traditional.

The lavish drawing room at night, now lit by candles or lamps. The curtains are drawn. The room is set for a confrontation, with family members positioned like a tableau. The atmosphere is tense and dramatic.

The interior hallway and landing of a Victorian girls' school at night. A staircase ascends into shadow. A closet door stands in the hallway. The scene is lit by the chaotic flickering of candles held by frightened residents. Sandwich bags and bonnets hang near the closet. The atmosphere is one of panic and confusion.

scenes.location_header: INT. MR. POTT'S GUEST ROOM - MORNING
scenes.visual_description: The same guest bedroom, now bright with morning sun. Through the window, the sounds of a brass band and shouting crowds drift in. A washstand with a pitcher and basin sits in the corner. Clothes are laid out on a chair. The mood is energetic and loud.

The same churchyard in the bright, cold light of Christmas morning. The sun shines on the snow-covered graves and the stone porch of the church. The frost has whitened a coat and lantern lying on the ground. The atmosphere is quiet, crisp, and realistic, stripped of the previous night's supernatural gloom.

Long, echoing stone galleries of the Fleet Prison. Rows of numbered doors line the walls. The air is heavy and damp. Shafts of grey light pierce the gloom from end windows. Figures flit to and fro like shadows. The atmosphere is restless and depressing.

A specially dirty room with a low ceiling and old panelled walls. Badly lighted, with great tallow candles burning despite the day. Crowds of attorneys and clerks jostle near a wooden bar. The atmosphere is noisy, stuffy, and chaotic.

A mean, poverty-stricken garret room in Camden Town. A bare deal table holds a miserable candle, casting long, dancing shadows. The walls are bare, damp, and peeling. The atmosphere is terrified, claustrophobic, and terminal, smelling of neglect.

A gentleman's study at night, cluttered with books and philosophical instruments. A writing desk holds a bottle of claret and a manuscript. A window looks out into complete darkness. Candlelight illuminates the serious face of a scholar. 1820s decor.
A quiet, nondescript room in a City tavern or coffee house. A simple table is covered with papers and receipts. The atmosphere is private and business-like, a refuge from the busy streets. 1827.

A maze of tortuous, narrow passages and staircases within the old inn. Rows of closed doors are garnished with boots. The area is pitch dark, relieved only by the faint glow of a dying candle or the moon through a window. The atmosphere is confusing, claustrophobic, and endless.

A large, desolate room in a ruined house. The roof has partially fallen in, revealing the night sky. A huge, blackened fireplace dominates one wall, filled with white ash. The floor is covered in debris. The atmosphere is cold, shadowy, and threatening, with a sense of former grandeur now lost to decay.

The grand entrance hall of a townhouse in Queen Square, Bath. A massive mahogany umbrella-stand is a prominent feature. The floor is polished stone. A heavy door leads to the street. The decor is ostentatious and wealthy Georgian. The atmosphere is haughty and silent.

scenes.location_header: EXT. FIELDS NEAR FORT PITT - DUSK
scenes.visual_description: A secluded grassy field near military fortifications at sunset. The sky is dull and heavy with grey clouds. In the background, the angular earthworks of a fort are visible. A wooden fence and hedge line the perimeter. The light is dimming, creating a sombre, melancholic atmosphere suitable for a duel. A lonely wind ripples the grass.

scenes.location_header: INT. SERJEANT SNUBBIN'S OUTER OFFICE - DAY
scenes.visual_description: An uncarpeted, dusty anteroom in Lincoln's Inn. A large writing-table with a green baize top, now gray with age and ink-stains, dominates the space. Bundles of papers tied with red tape are everywhere. The atmosphere is severe, ancient, and exceedingly legal.

The 'Poor Side' of the Fleet Prison. A wretched, bare room with rough stone walls. A dusty fire smoulders in the grate. The furniture consists of broken boxes and a few rags. The atmosphere is one of abject misery and hopelessness. Tattered garments and starvation define the scene.

scenes.location_header: EXT. TOWN ARMS STABLE YARD - DAY
scenes.visual_description: View from an upper window looking down into a stable yard crowded with people. Blue flags wave vigorously. A wooden hustings platform stands in the center. The scene is packed with voters, constables, and musicians. Bright daylight illuminates the chaos.

scenes.location_header: INT. ANGEL INN GUEST SUITE - NIGHT
scenes.visual_description: A private guest suite at the Angel Inn, encompassing a sitting area and a bedroom alcove. A four-poster bed with heavy curtains dominates the background. A fireplace with dying embers casts a low light. A small table holds a candle. The atmosphere is quiet, concluding, and intimate.

A view from the box of a speeding mail coach at night. Dark trees and hedges blur past in a rush of motion. The four black horses are frothing and galloping furiously. The road stretches ahead, illuminated by the coach lamps. The atmosphere is frantic and high-velocity.

A magnificent Georgian ballroom and card-room suite in Bath. Crystal chandeliers cast brilliant light onto chalked floors and gilt mirrors. Card tables are set out in the side rooms. The atmosphere is crowded, glittering, and heavy with perfume and scandal. Rich fabrics and feathers are everywhere.

A bedroom identical in layout to the previous one, lit by a dying fire and a rushlight shade in a basin on the floor. Two beds with curtains. A dressing glass stands on a table. The room is shadowy and intimate. A sense of awkward privacy prevails.
